MERIDIAN GRID SECURITY PVT LTD Internal Operations Dossier Confidential — Compiled for Internal Review, Q3 FY2024-25

[Section: 1. Executive Summary | Page 2 | text]
1. Executive Summary Meridian Grid Security Pvt Ltd ("Meridian Grid") is a Mumbai-headquartered managed security and infrastructure-hardening firm serving mid-market retail, fintech, and logistics clients across South and Southeast Asia. This dossier consolidates the organization's operating history, personnel records, incident response log, vendor inventory, client deployment portfolio, risk register, and the findings of the most recent internal compliance audit. It is intended as a single reference document for leadership review ahead of the FY2024-25 board meeting. The company has grown from a three-person consultancy in 2019 to a 41-person operation as of this

[Section: 1. Executive Summary | Page 2 | text]
The company has grown from a three-person consultancy in 2019 to a 41-person operation as of this writing, with a dedicated Security Operations Center (SOC) handling both proactive monitoring and incident response for eleven active client deployments. Over the review period, the SOC logged six reportable incidents of varying severity, none of which resulted in confirmed data exfiltration, though two triggered mandatory client notification under contractual SLAs. This document deliberately consolidates information that in normal operations lives across separate systems — HR records, the incident tracker, the vendor management platform, the client CRM, and the

[Section: 1. Executive Summary | Page 2 | text]
systems — HR records, the incident tracker, the vendor management platform, the client CRM, and the audit findings register — into one file, so that any single question about the business may require checking more than one section.

[Section: 2. Company Background & Timeline | Page 3 | text]
2. Company Background & Timeline Meridian Grid was founded in April 2019 by Aarav Mehta, previously a network security lead at a Bengaluru-based payments processor. The company was incorporated with two additional co-founders handling business development and finance respectively, though neither remains with the company today. Meridian Grid's first office was a shared workspace in Andheri East, Mumbai; the company relocated to a dedicated office in Powai in early 2021 as headcount crossed fifteen. The founding thesis of the business was that mid-market companies in India and neighboring markets

[Section: 2. Company Background & Timeline | Page 3 | text]
The founding thesis of the business was that mid-market companies in India and neighboring markets were underserved by security vendors who typically focus on large enterprise accounts, and that a leaner, retainer-based model combining penetration testing, SOC-as-a-service, and infrastructure hardening could capture that segment profitably.

2.1 Timeline of Major Milestones

[Section: 2.1 Timeline of Major Milestones | Page 3 | table]
Year: 2019; Milestone: Company founded; first client (a regional logistics firm) onboarded in June 2019.
Year: 2020; Milestone: Remote-first SOC model adopted during the pandemic; headcount reaches 9.
Year: 2021; Milestone: Office relocated to Powai; first enterprise-tier client (Vantage Retail Group) signed.
Year: 2022; Milestone: ISO 27001 certification achieved; SOC begins 24x7 shift coverage.
Year: 2023; Milestone: Expansion into Southeast Asia with a Singapore-registered subsidiary.

The company's fiscal year runs April to March. All monetary figures in this dossier are in Indian Rupees (INR) unless otherwise stated.

[Section: 3. Organizational Structure & Personnel History | Page 4 | text]
3. Organizational Structure & Personnel History Meridian Grid operates a flat structure below the founder level, with four functional leads reporting directly to the CEO: Head of Security, Head of Client Delivery, Head of Engineering, and Head of Finance & Operations. The Head of Security role has particular relevance to this dossier as it owns both the incident response function and the vendor risk sign-off process described in later sections.

[Section: 3.1 Head of Security — Historical Tenure | Page 4 | text]
3.1 Head of Security — Historical Tenure Naina Kapoor served as the founding Head of Security from the company's incorporation in April 2019 until her departure in August 2021 to join a venture-backed startup. She was succeeded by Rohan Bhatt, who had previously been a senior SOC analyst at the company since 2020 and was promoted internally. Rohan Bhatt continues to hold the Head of Security role as of this writing.

[Section: 4. Incident Response Log (January 2022 – August 2024) | Page 5 | text]
INC-003 (April 2023) remains the single costliest incident in company history and triggered a mandatory client notification. It occurred during a planned VPN migration for a retail client when a firewall rule intended to be temporary was left in an overly permissive state for eleven days, exposing an internal inventory management endpoint. INC-004 (September 2023) was not caused by Meridian Grid's own misconfiguration but by a breach at a third-party API vendor integrated into a client's stack; this incident is referenced again in Section 7 in connection with audit findings on vendor risk.

Following INC-003, the Engineering team developed an internal tool, the Firewall Rule Auto-Validator v2, which flags temporary firewall rules that have not been reverted within a configurable time window. This tool is referenced again in Section 5 in connection with client deployments.

[Section: 6. Risk Register & Severity Weighting Methodology | Page 7 | text]
6. Risk Register & Severity Weighting Methodology Meridian Grid's internal risk register assigns a numeric weight to each severity tier used in the incident log (Section 4). This weighting is used internally for quarterly risk reporting to translate raw incident cost into a "severity-weighted cost" figure, which the Finance and Security functions use jointly to prioritize remediation investment. The methodology was formalized in 2022 following the ISO 27001 certification process and has not changed since.

[Section: 6.1 Severity Weight Table | Page 7 | text]
6.1 Severity Weight Table

[Section: 6.1 Severity Weight Table | Page 7 | table]
Severity Tier: Low; Weight Multiplier: 1.0x; Definition: Contained, no client impact, no notification required.
Severity Tier: Medium; Weight Multiplier: 1.5x; Definition: Limited client impact, internal remediation only.
Severity Tier: High; Weight Multiplier: 2.0x; Definition: Client-facing impact, remediation within SLA window.
Severity Tier: Critical; Weight Multiplier: 4.0x; Definition: Client notification mandatory, board-level visibility.

[Section: 6.1 Severity Weight Table | Page 7 | text]
The severity-weighted cost for a given incident is calculated as the reconciled cost (Section 4) multiplied by the weight multiplier for its severity tier. This figure is reported quarterly per root-cause category so leadership can see which categories of failure carry the greatest weighted exposure, not merely the highest raw cost. As a matter of policy, the weighting table above is reviewed annually by the Head of Security and Head of Finance jointly and requires CEO sign-off to change; no changes have been made since the table's adoption in 2022, meaning it applies uniformly across all incidents listed in Section 4 regardless of when in the review period they occurred.

[Section: 8. Compliance Audit Findings — Q3 FY2024-25 | Page 9 | text]
8. Compliance Audit Findings — Q3 FY2024-25 An internal compliance audit was conducted in Q3 FY2024-25 by an external auditor engaged by the Head of Finance, covering data handling practices, vendor risk management, and incident response documentation. The audit produced four findings, summarized below in order of severity as rated by the auditor.

[Section: 8.1 Finding 1 — Vendor Data Residency Risk (High) | Page 9 | text]
8.1 Finding 1 — Vendor Data Residency Risk (High) The audit found that CloudSentry API, the threat intelligence vendor listed in Section 7, processes client telemetry data on infrastructure located outside India without a data processing agreement that satisfies Meridian Grid's contractual data residency commitments to two clients. This finding is directly connected to the vendor's prior involvement in INC-004 (Section 4) and has been escalated for contract renegotiation or replacement within two quarters.

[Section: 8.2 Finding 2 — Incident Documentation Gaps (Medium) | Page 9 | text]
8.2 Finding 2 — Incident Documentation Gaps (Medium) Two of the six incidents in the review period (INC-002 and INC-005) lacked a completed post-incident review document within the company's mandated 10-business-day window, though both were eventually completed.

[Section: 8.3 Finding 3 — On-Call Roster Redundancy (Medium) | Page 9 | text]
8.3 Finding 3 — On-Call Roster Redundancy (Medium) The auditor noted that only four engineers are on the senior on-call roster (Section 3.2) for a 14-person SOC function, creating single points of failure during simultaneous incidents. This finding did not reference any specific incident in the log.

[Section: 8.4 Finding 4 — Access Review Cadence (Low) | Page 9 | text]
8.4 Finding 4 — Access Review Cadence (Low) Quarterly access reviews for the SentinelWatch SIEM platform (Section 7) were found to be conducted on an inconsistent cadence, with one quarter skipped in FY2023-24.

Reportable event: any SOC-logged incident meeting the threshold for inclusion in the quarterly board
